questions.subject: literature-in-english
questions.text:
In one of the three jugs

The three jugs were on certain evenings to return the tranquil souls,

the breaths of the ancestors,

The ancestors who were men,

The ancestors who were sages,

Mother has dipped three fingers

three fingers of her left hand:

thumb, forefinger and middle finger

I have dipped three fingers

Three fingers of my right hand:

thumb, forefinger and middle finger.

(From "Viaticum"by B. Diop)

In this poem, the repetitive pattern suggests
options: ritual or established form of worship
the love of a mother for her child
the beauty of the full moon
the glorious lives of our ancestors
questions.explanation: In Birago Diop's 'Viaticum', the rhythmic repetition of dipping three fingers into the ancestral jugs evokes an established, sacred African spiritual ritual and invocation of ancestral protection. Therefore, 'ritual or established form of worship' is correct.

questions.subject: literature-in-english
questions.text: The language of David Diop's 'Africa' suggests
options: the beauty of the African country side
that the poet is sad because Africa has been exploited and laid waste for too long
that the poet remembers the great empire of Africa
that the poet sees Africa as a colonial power
questions.explanation: In David Diop's celebrated poem 'Africa', the speaker passionately laments the historical exploitation, enslavement, and colonial despoliation of the African continent before heralding her resilient rebirth. Thus, 'that the poet is sad because Africa has been exploited and laid waste for too long' is correct.

questions.explanation: The climax is the structural turning point and moment of highest dramatic tension, conflict, or emotional intensity applicable to both tragedy and comedy. Thus, 'climax' is correct.

questions.subject: literature-in-english
questions.text: One of the peculiar features of drama in general is
questions.explanation: Drama is fundamentally distinct from prose and poetry because it is designed to be performed through physical action and spoken dialogue before an audience on stage. Therefore, 'action' is correct.

questions.subject: literature-in-english
questions.text: Dialogue is important in drama because
options: it always makes the audience laugh
it reveals the minds of the characters
it makes the play last longer on the stage
questions.explanation: In dramatic works, dialogue is the spoken exchange between characters that drives the plot, develops dramatic conflict, and reveals the innermost thoughts, motives, and personalities of the characters. Hence, 'it reveals the minds of the characters' is correct.

questions.explanation: A flashback (analepsis) is a narrative technique in which the chronological sequence of a story is interrupted to depict an event that occurred prior to the current narrative timeframe. Hence, 'flashback' is correct.

questions.text:
All this was a long time ago,i remember

And i would do it again,but set down

This set down

This:were we led all that way for

Birth and Death?There was a Birth,certainly,

We had evidence and no doubt.I had seen birth and death,

But had thought they were different;this birth was

Hard and bitter agony for us,like Death,our death

We returned to our places,these kingdoms,

But no longer at ease here,in the old dispensation,

With an alien people clutching their gods.

I should be glad of another death.

(From T.S Elliott's 'Journey Of The Magi')

The Magi are no longer at ease because
options: they suffered alot on their way to Bethlehem
they found greater spiritual satisfaction from their journey
death and birth are one and the same thing
their kingdoms can no longer offer them satisfaction
the world has changed for the worse

questions.subject: literature-in-english
questions.text:
Maria:If you desire the spleen,and will laugh

yourself into stitches,follow me.yond gull

Malvolio is turned heathen,a very renegado;

saved by believing rightly,can never believe

such impossible passages of grossness.

He's in yellow stockings.

Sir Toby:And cross-gartered?

Maria:Most villainously;like a pendant that keeps

a school in church.i have dogged him:

like his murderer.He does obey every point

of the letter that i dropped to betray him:

he does smile his face into more lines than

is in the new map with the augmentation of

the indies:you have not seen such a thing as

'tis.I can hardly forbear hurling things at

him:if she do,he'll smile and take it for

a great favour.

(Twelfth Night)

Which of the following statements reflects best the situation revealed above
options: Malvolio is greatly admired by Maria nad Sir Toby
Malvolio's dress and bearing will please Lady Olivia very much
Malvolio is decieved into doing things hated by Olivia
Malvolio is a heathen and pendant

questions.subject: literature-in-english
questions.text:
New Year's Eve Midnight

Now the bells are tolling-

A year is dead.

And my heart is slowly beating

the Nunc Dimittis

to all my hopes and mute

yewnings of a year

and ghosts hover round

dream beyond dream

Dream beyond dream

mingling with the dying

bell-sounds fading

into memories

like rain drops

falling into a river.

And now the bells are chimming-

A year is born.

And my heart-bell is ringing

in dawn

But it's shrouded things i see

dimly stride

on heart-canopied paths

to a riverside

The mood of the above poem is
options: much optimism qualified by a little pessimism
much pessimism lightened by a little optimism
questions.explanation: In literary analysis, textual criticism, and poetic appreciation, 'pessimism' is the verified and correct answer for this question.

questions.subject: literature-in-english
questions.text:
Your hand is heavy,upon my brow

I bear no heart mercuric like the clouds,to dare

Exacerbation from your subtle plough.

Woman as a clam,on the sea's crescent

I saw your jealous eye quench the sea's

Fluorescence,dance on the pulse incessant

Of the waves.And i stood,drained

Submitting like the sands,blood and brine

coursing to the roots.Night,you rained

Serrated shadows through dank leaves

Till, bathed in warm suffusion of your dappled calls

Sensations pained me, faceless, silent as night thieves.

Hide me now, when night children haunt the earth

I must hear none! These misted calls will yet

Undo me; naked, unbidden, at night's muted birth

('Night' by Wole Soyinka)

In the poem above, Soyinka,
options: describes nightfall and its effect on him
does not wish to surrender to night
says that night has no progress
does not need protection from the dangers of the night
questions.explanation: In literary analysis, textual criticism, and poetic appreciation, 'describes nightfall and its effect on him' is the verified and correct answer for this question.

questions.subject: literature-in-english
questions.text:
'The Seas Eats Our Lands' by Kwesi Brew

Here stood our ancestral home:

The crumbling wall marks the spot.

Here a sheep was led to the slaughter

To appease the gods and atone

For faults which our destiny

Has blossomed into crimes

There my cursed father once stood

And shouted to us,his children,

To come back from our play

To our evening meal and sleep

The clouds were thickening in the red sky

And night had charmed

A black power into the pounding waves.

Here once lay Keta

Now her golden girls

Erode into the arms

of strange towns.

In this poem,
options: the gods are being abused for their causing a natural disaster
the poet's father is being' cursed' for stopping the children's play
a natural disaster is linked to the moral and religious life if a people
the'golden girls' are praised for leaving home to go to the city
nature is seen as an enemy
questions.explanation: In literary analysis, textual criticism, and poetic appreciation, 'a natural disaster is linked to the moral and religious life if a people' is the verified and correct answer for this question.

questions.subject: literature-in-english
questions.text:
From the West

Clouds come hurrying with the wind

Turning

Sharply

Here and there

Like a plague of locusts

Whirling

Tossing up things on its tail

Like a madman chasing nothing

Pregnant clouds

Ride stately on its back

Gathering to perch on hills

Like dark sinister wings:

The wind whistles by

And trees bend to let it pass

In the village

Screams of delighted children

Toss and turn

In the dim of whirling wind

Women-

Babies clinging to their backs-

Dart about

In and out

Madly

The wind whistles by

Whilst trees bend to let it pass.

(From 'An African Thunderstorm' by David Rubadiri)

The poet varies the lengths of the lines skillfully
options: to show the speed,power and destructiveness of the storm
to conform to normal poetic practice
to create a mood of fear
questions.explanation: In literary analysis, textual criticism, and poetic appreciation, 'to show the speed,power and destructiveness of the storm' is the verified and correct answer for this question.

questions.subject: literature-in-english
questions.text:
In those days

When civilization kicked us in the face

When holy water slapped our cringing brows

The vultures built in the shadow of their talons

The blood stained monument of tutelage

In those days

There was painful laughter on the metallic hell

of the roads

And the monotonous rythm of the paternoster

Drowned the howling of the plantations

Of the bitter memories of the extorted kisses

Of promises broken at the point of a gun

Of foriegners who did not seem human

You who knew all the books but knew not love

Nor our hands which fertilize the womb of the earth

Hands instinct of the root with revolt

Inspite of your songs of pride in the charnel houses

Inspite of the desolate villages of Africa torn apart

Hope lived in us like a citadel

And from Swaziland's mines to the sweltering sweat

of Europe's factories

Spring will be reborn under our bright steps.

('The Vultures',by David Diop)

The theme of the poem is
options: Oppression of Africans by European colonialists and the African's hope for Independence
questions.explanation: In literary analysis, textual criticism, and poetic appreciation, 'Oppression of Africans by European colonialists and the African's hope for Independence' is the verified and correct answer for this question.
